title: Design a table

outcomes.can: Create a table with types, a key and a default.
Predict which rows a constraint rejects.
Link a table to another with a foreign key.

intro: A table's definition decides what data it will accept. Types, keys and constraints written into the definition reject bad rows before they are stored, so no query has to work around them later. This module covers CREATE TABLE and the constraints that protect a table.

steps.title: Columns, types and a key
steps.text: CREATE TABLE names a table and lists its columns. Each column has a name and a type: integer for whole numbers, numeric(8, 2) for exact decimals with two places, text, boolean, date. After the type come the column's rules. PRIMARY KEY marks the column that identifies a row. Its values must be unique and cannot be NULL. NOT NULL means the column must always have a value. DEFAULT gives the value to use when an INSERT leaves the column out. UNIQUE forbids two rows with the same value.

steps.title: Leave a column out
steps.text: The INSERT gives no country. Predict what the row holds for it.

steps.title: Read the stored row
steps.text: The row was stored with country USA, the column's default. The rating was given as 4. A column with no default and no value would hold NULL, which is allowed only when the column is not NOT NULL.

steps.title: Rules about values
steps.text: CHECK attaches a test to the table. A row is accepted only when the test is not false. CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5) rejects a rating of 9. A check that involves a NULL value is unknown, not false, so the row is accepted. Add NOT NULL when the column must be filled in.

steps.title: Break a CHECK
steps.text: The table allows ratings from 1 to 5. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Read the error
steps.text: Check the example. Error 23514 says the new row violates a check constraint. The row is not stored. A constraint is a guarantee: every row that is in the table has passed it.

steps.title: Rules about other tables
steps.text: REFERENCES links a column to the key of another table. order_id integer REFERENCES orders (id) is a foreign key. It accepts only values that exist as an id in orders. It also protects the other side: an order cannot be deleted while a row still points at it.

steps.title: Point at a missing row
steps.text: No product has id 999. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Create a suppliers table
steps.text: The starter creates the table with no rules at all. Add them.

steps.title: Create a shipments table
steps.text: Work from the prompt. One column points at another table and one has a limit.

questions.prompt: What does the stored row hold for country?

choices.feedback: The INSERT left country out, so its default was used.
The column has a default, so a missing value becomes USA.
A NOT NULL column with a default accepts an INSERT that leaves it out.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.text: The row is stored with a rating of 5.
choices.feedback: A constraint never changes a value. It accepts the row or rejects it.

choices.text: The row is stored with a rating of 9.
choices.feedback: 9 is outside 1 to 5, so the CHECK rejects the row.

choices.text: PostgreSQL reports an error and stores nothing.
choices.feedback: The rating fails the CHECK, so the row is rejected (23514).

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.text: The item is added with product 999.
choices.feedback: A foreign key accepts only ids that exist in the other table.

choices.text: PostgreSQL reports an error and stores nothing.
choices.feedback: product_id must match an existing product, and none has id 999 (23503).

choices.text: A product with id 999 is created.
choices.feedback: A foreign key checks the other table. It never adds rows to it.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one constraint each. They do not test a table against rows that should be rejected.
